questions.prompt: A receiver parses and reserializes a signed JSON body before verification. What should it do instead?

options.label: Verify the exact received bytes with the configured endpoint secret before trusting parsed fields.
Whitespace changes never affect a signature over raw bytes.
Choose a signing secret using an unauthenticated body field.

questions.explanation: Raw-byte integrity covers the received representation. Trusted endpoint/account configuration selects the verifier; parsed data does not authorize the secret choice.

questions.prompt: A valid old payload is replayed with a newer timestamp supplied by the sender. What must the verifier establish?

options.label: Authenticate the timestamp and check the configured clock tolerance; replay prevention also needs durable deduplication.
Check only that the supplied timestamp looks recent.
A valid signature means every later replay should cause a new effect.

questions.explanation: The timestamp must be part of the authenticated message. Freshness narrows replay time but does not prevent duplicate deliveries inside that interval.

questions.prompt: The provider retries an already accepted event with a fresh valid signature. Is it a new business event?

options.label: Verify each delivery, then consult a scoped event receipt; a fresh signature does not make the event new.
Use the signature value as the stable event identifier.
Skip signature verification whenever the body contains a familiar event ID.

questions.explanation: A delivery attempt and event identity differ. Verify first, then deduplicate against the configured account/endpoint scope and durable receipt policy.

questions.prompt: The toy returns accepted and stores an event in its in-memory set. What is still needed before a production receiver promises reliable effects?

options.label: Acknowledge durable acceptance, process idempotently and reconcile failures; an in-memory seen set cannot prove crash-safe effects.
A set plus 200 response proves exactly-once payments after process crashes.
Mark the event completed before durable admission so failures can be ignored.

questions.explanation: The set models admission only. Real acknowledgment follows the chosen durable acceptance boundary; external effects and local receipts require idempotency/reconciliation.
